conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: GENERATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format: GENERATE {data-name-1 | report-name-1} (cite.py --check 14.9.16.2 "GENERATE" OK). The grammar parses one operand, `GENERATE reportGroupReference` = cobolWord [(IN|OF) reportName]. The optional qualifier is SR1's "It may be qualified by a report-name". BindGenerate tells the two alternatives apart by resolution. An unqualified name that resolves to a report is report-name-1 (summary reporting); otherwise it resolves through ReportGroupResolution to a report group (data-name-1). A name that matches neither is COBOLNET1757. Both alternatives were compiled and run in probe out/probe/generate/g1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): `GENERATE DE-1` and `GENERATE R-1`. The data-name alternative is also exercised by conformance:2023/pb365_report_group_qualified and 85/pb365_report_group_qualified_85, which include the qualified form. No spec-derived test exercises the report-name alternative, so test-ref is left empty. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Report Writer is present in every edition; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to GENERATE)

rows.subject: GENERATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR2: "Report-name-1 may be used only if the referenced report description entry contains a CONTROL clause." (cite.py --check 14.9.16.3 OK, 2)). BindGenerate reports ReportGenerateNeedsControl when summary.Controls.Count == 0. Probe out/probe/generate/g2.cob (no CONTROL clause) was rejected at both 85 and 2023 at each GENERATE R-1. With a CONTROL clause, g1.cob compiles and runs. Both halves of the rule were verified. The diagnostic is issued under COBOLNET0899, the 'recognized but not implemented' code, so an illegal program is reported as a compiler limitation. Open note PB1028 already owns that code-category defect, so it is not re-reported here. No negative golden exists, so test-ref is empty. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Report Writer is present in every edition; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to GENERATE)
rows.rule-text: Report-name-1 may be used only if the referenced report description entry contains a CONTROL clause.

rows.subject: GENERATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR2: GENERATE report-name-1 "results in the same processing as for a GENERATE data-name statement for the same report, except that no detail is printed. This process is called summary reporting." (cite.py --check 14.9.16.4 OK, 2)). BindGenerate returns BoundGenerate(summary, null) and the emitter passes null to Generate. GenerateCore runs the same GR4/GR5 control-break path and the same SUM accumulation. Only the final `detailName is not null` presentation is skipped. probe out/probe/generate/g1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): a summary GENERATE R-1 with no control break printed nothing. A summary GENERATE R-1 after K1 changed 2->3 printed CF2 21, CF1 21, CH1 31, CH2 31 and no DE line, which matches the spec. The second sentence only defines the term 'summary report' and has no operational content. No spec-derived test exercises summary reporting, so test-ref is empty. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Report Writer is present in every edition; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to GENERATE)
rows.rule-text: Execution of a GENERATE report-name-1 statement results in the same processing as for a GENERATE data-name statement for the same report, except that no detail is printed. This process is called summary reporting. If all the GENERATE statements executed for a report between the execution of the INITIATE and TERMINATE statements are of this form, the report that is produced is called a summary report.

rows.subject: GLOBAL clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "If the GLOBAL clause is used in a data description entry that contains the REDEFINES clause, it is only the subject of that REDEFINES clause that possesses the global attribute." (cite.py --check 13.18.27.4 -> OK GR3). The scan registers only the entry whose own clause list carries GLOBAL. Probe p2 (01 A; 01 B REDEFINES A GLOBAL): containee reference to A -> COBOLNET1639 while B resolves. Probe p3 (01 A GLOBAL; 01 B REDEFINES A): containee reference to B -> COBOLNET1639. Both directions verified. No spec-derived test exists (test-needed). || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: If the GLOBAL clause is used in a data description entry that contains the REDEFINES clause, it is only the subject of that REDEFINES clause that possesses the global attribute.

rows.subject: GROUP INDICATE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: General format '<u>GROUP</u> INDICATE' — only GROUP is underlined, so INDICATE is an optional word. Grammar: reportGroupIndicateClause : GROUP INDICATE? ; admitted as an alternative of reportGroupClause (any order within the entry). Probes probe/group-indicate-clause/gip1..gip6 parse 'GROUP INDICATE' in any clause position. No edition gate needed: the clause is in every edition's report writer. cite.py --check 13.18.28.3 'may be specified only within a detail report group description' OK (the clause family). No spec-derived golden exercises the clause (pb565_report_repeating_entry mentions it only in a comment; ReportWriterSpecTests.GroupIndicate_PrintsOncePerGroup is in the legacy CobolSharp.Tests.Integration project) — test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985 (Report Writer module), 2002, 2014, 2023

rows.subject: General
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format: ACCESS MODE IS {SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC}, ACCESS/SEQUENTIAL/RANDOM/DYNAMIC underlined, MODE and IS optional words (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.1 "ACCESS" -> OK). Grammar accessModeClause : ACCESS MODE? IS? accessMode; accessMode : SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC -- exact match. DataBinder.BindFileControl maps it via MapAccessMode onto FileModel.AccessMode. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 85 and 2023): 'ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS RANDOM', 'ACCESS IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL' all accepted and honoured (gA.cob, gB.cob); 'ACCESS MODE IS' with no mode rejected COBOL0312 (gE.cob); 'MODE IS RANDOM' without ACCESS rejected COBOL0312 (gF.cob). SIBLING (not this row): the FD grammar fileDescriptionClause (CobolData.g4:69-71) also admits organizationClause/accessModeClause/recordKeyClause, which §13.4.5.2's closed formats do not, and nothing reads them -- 'FD SQ ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC.' compiles and runs silently as a plain sequential file (gG.cob, gH.cob); reported as a finding against FMT-13.4.5.2. No spec-derived golden targets the clause's format variants, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
rows.rule-text:
╭ SEQUENTIAL ╮ │ │ ACCESS MODE IS ┤ RANDOM ├ │ │ ╰ DYNAMIC ╯
> **Figure notes (ACCESS MODE clause syntax diagram).** `ACCESS`, `SEQUENTIAL`, `RANDOM`, and `DYNAMIC` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `MODE` and `IS` are **not** underlined. The braces are plain — exactly one of the three access modes shall be selected.

rows.subject: General
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, sequential access is assumed." (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.3 -> OK §12.4.5.5.3 1)). FileModel.AccessMode defaults to FileAccessMode.Sequential (FileModel.cs:128) and is only overwritten by a written clause (DataBinder.cs:994); the ordinal passes to the runtime KeyedAccess.Sequential=0. Probe gA.cob: INDEXED file with no ACCESS clause, WRITE 'C3' then 'A1' -> statuses 00 then 21 (sequence error, the sequential-access indexed WRITE rule), proving sequential access was assumed; gB.cob: RELATIVE with no ACCESS clause reads records in ascending RRN (R2,R5,R9) with plain READ. Both at --std 85 and 2023. No spec-derived golden asserts the default specifically. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
rows.rule-text: If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, sequential access is assumed.

rows.subject: General
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule has three parts (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.3 OK for 2) a), 2) b), 2) c)). All three verified by probe at --std 85 and 2023: a) sequential file written S2,S1 then OPEN EXTEND S0 reads back S2,S1,S0 -- predecessor-successor order of the WRITEs at creation and extension (gB.cob); b) relative file written RANDOM at RRN 5,2,9 reads back sequentially R2,R5,R9 -- ascending RRN of existing records, gaps skipped (gB.cob); c) indexed file written DYNAMIC C1,A3,B2 reads back sequentially A3,B2,C1 on the prime key, and after START on the alternate key C1,B2,A3 -- ascending within the key of reference (gA.cob); the collating-sequence half of c) is covered by conformance:2002/pb703_collating_key_named_twice and conformance:2002/file_collating_seq (both derive expected output from §12.4.5.5.3 GR2 c) and §12.4.5.7.4), IndexedConnector.cs:755 cites GR2c. test-ref left empty because no single spec-derived golden covers a) and b) as well as c). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
rows.rule-text: If the access mode is sequential, records in the file are accessed in the sequence dictated by the file organization: a) For sequential files this sequence is specified by predecessor-successor record relationships established by the execution of WRITE statements when the physical file is created or extended. b) For relative files this sequence is the order of ascending relative record numbers of existing records in the physical file. c) For indexed files this sequence is ascending within a given key of reference according to the collating sequence for that key.

rows.subject: General
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.3 OK for 3) a) and 3) b)): under random access, a) relative: the relative key data item selects the record; b) indexed: the record key data item selects it. KeyedIoBinder maps FileAccessMode.Random to ReadKind.Random (KeyedIoBinder.cs:73). Probes at --std 85 and 2023: a) RELATIVE ACCESS RANDOM, RK=9 READ -> 'R9' status 00; RK=3 (no record) -> INVALID KEY status 23 (gB.cob). b) INDEXED ACCESS RANDOM, IXR-KEY='B' READ -> 'B2'; 'Z' -> INVALID KEY 23 (gA.cob). Random WRITE by relative key (RRN 5,2,9 out of order) also lands each record at its key (gB.cob). Both halves verified. No spec-derived golden cited for this rule. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
rows.rule-text: If the access mode is random: a) For a relative file, the value of a relative key data item indicates the record to be accessed. b) For an indexed file, the value of a record key data item indicates the record to be accessed.

rows.subject: General
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "If the access mode is dynamic, records in the file may be accessed sequentially, randomly, or both." (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.3 -> OK §12.4.5.5.3 4)). Probes at --std 85 and 2023: INDEXED DYNAMIC -- random WRITEs out of key order succeed (C1,A3,B2 status 00), READ KEY IS IXD-KEY='B' -> B2 00, then READ NEXT -> C1 00 (gA.cob); RELATIVE ACCESS IS DYNAMIC -- RK=2 random READ -> R2 00, READ NEXT -> R5 00 with RK updated to 05 (gB.cob). Both sequential and random access, mixed on one open, work for both keyed organizations. No spec-derived golden cited. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
rows.rule-text: If the access mode is dynamic, records in the file may be accessed sequentially, randomly, or both.

rows.subject: Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §8.3.3.2.4 5) (cite.py OK) leaves the no-corresponding-character result to the implementor. DecodeHex maps each 2-digit group to (char)0x00hh; HexGroupViolation refuses a partial group per §8.3.3.2.3 6) (cite.py OK). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p95.cob at 2014/2023: X"80FF0041" ORD 129 256 1 66, LENGTH 4; p95b.cob DISPLAY X"80FF41" prints U+0080 U+00FF 'A' (UTF-8 C2 80 C3 BF 41). Every group has a character, so the row states the case cannot arise. No spec-derived test pins the high-range values; test-ref empty. Closes the item-95 documentation gap owned by kb/Work/PB1397.
rows.rule-text: Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.3.3.2, Alphanumeric literals, General rule 4)

rows.subject: Hexadecimal national literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §8.3.3.5.4 5) (cite.py OK) leaves the no-corresponding-character result to the implementor; §8.3.3.5.3 5) (cite.py OK) the digits per character. DecodeHexGroups(digits,4) casts each group to a char. Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p95.cob: NX"D800FFFF0041" ORD 55297 65536 66, LENGTH(NX"D800")=1; p97.cob: NX"D800DC00" into N(2) gives ORD 55297 56321 (two positions), NX"FFFF" > NX"D800" true, DISPLAY of lone DC00 writes EF BF BD (U+FFFD), exit 0. No spec-derived test pins the no-character arm (r03_hexadecimal_national_and_boolean_literals pins only NX"00410042"), so test-ref empty. Closes the documentation gap PB160 names for item 97.
